# `type` for [core](/commands/categories/core.md)

<div class='command-title'>Give a name to a type annotation.</div>

## Command Type

`keyword`

## Signature

```> type {flags} (name) (type)```

## Parameters

 -  `name`: Name of the type alias.
 -  `type`: Equals sign followed by a type, as written after `:` on a parameter.


## Input/output types:

| input   | output  |
| ------- | ------- |
| nothing | nothing |
## Examples

Name a record type and use it for a parameter and an output type.
```nu
> type Point = record<x: int, y: int>
    def shift [p: Point]: nothing -> Point { {x: ($p.x + 1), y: $p.y} }
    (shift {x: 1, y: 2}).x
2
```

Build a type from another type alias.
```nu
> type Point = record<x: int, y: int>
    type Segment = record<from: Point, to: Point>
    def width [s: Segment]: nothing -> int { $s.to.x - $s.from.x }
    width {from: {x: 1, y: 0}, to: {x: 4, y: 2}}
3
```

Give a parameter of an aliased type a completer.
```nu
> type Color = string
    def paint [color: Color@[red green blue]] { $"painting it ($color)" }
    paint red
painting it red
```

## Notes
This command is a parser keyword. The parser replaces the name with its type wherever the name is used as a type: in parameters, input/output types, variable annotations and other types. The alias is visible from its definition to the end of the block.

A completer belongs to a parameter, not to its type, so `type` takes no `@completer`. Write it on the parameter instead, as in `color: Color@[red green blue]`.

`type` is reserved, so a custom command or alias can't be named `type`. To run an external `type` command, use `^type`.

For details, check:
  https://www.nushell.sh/book/thinking_in_nu.html
